title: Italiano in ospedale — sintomi, corpo, dottore
subtitle: Medical Italian for speaking with doctors and nurses in Italy
source_summary: User-requested cross-domain lesson on Italian medical vocabulary for hospital communication. Covers body parts, common symptoms, and patient-doctor dialogue patterns. Designed for travelers and visitors who may need to navigate Italian healthcare. Cross-domain test for the chiron pipeline (language-it + medical context).
learning_objectives: Master 14 medical/body verbs (avere male, sentire, soffrire, respirare, tossire, ...) and their conjugation in 4 daily tenses.
Use 15 body-part nouns with correct articles (la testa, il petto, lo stomaco, ...).
Describe a symptom using fare male / avere mal di / sentire dolore.
Handle a triage conversation at pronto soccorso (ER) in Italian.
Recognize core hospital signage (uscita, pronto soccorso, farmacia, dottore, infermiera).
Build automaticity via Match Madness across vocab, gender, prepositions, collocations, and tenses.
authentic_sources_used: Italian patient information leaflets (foglietto illustrativo) — public-domain
Italian National Health Service (Servizio Sanitario Nazionale) signage standards
